hook: SCP-1867 is a small, funny article about a sea slug with the manners and memories of a Victorian adventurer. It is short and light, and the joke works best if you simply let the gentleman talk. Expect pulp-era exploration stories filtered through a very unlikely narrator.
whyItMatters: Lord Blackwood has his own tag, which tells you the character outgrew this one file and became a recurring comic voice on the site. The article also uses an esoteric-class style header, with a structured containment block replacing the usual Safe or Euclid line. It shows how much personality an entry can carry while the actual anomaly stays tiny.
thingsToNotice:
The containment procedure is not about the slug at all; it is a rule for fact-checking its stories, which neatly tells you where the real risk lies. The recovered collection then complicates the joke, since a vault full of impossible specimens suggests at least some of the tall tales were true.

Watch the small absurd details in the inventory, like the planetary globes and the carriage with a note about it being broken. The interview ends on a perfect reversal, with the slug treating the researcher as the one who has lost his grip.

related.note: Another genial entity whose claims about itself are impossible to pin down.
A lighter entry where the comedy comes from deadpan Foundation reporting.
